newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent Chicago prices firm on outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent Chicago prices firm on outage.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel prices were driven higher on Monday in Chicago by refiner buying sparked by a weekend fire at a key regional refinery, traders said.

Clark Refining & Marketing Co was sighted in the market for spot diesel and premium unleaded barrels after a fire on Saturday idled a 6,400 barrel per day alkylation unit at its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., traders said.
The company expects the alkylation unit, which produces premium unleaded gasoline, to be back in service later this week, a refinery spokeswoman said.

Traders said Colonial Pipeline Co's decision to freeze 29th cycle distillate shipments and prorate shipments for cycles through November was dampening Gulf coast differentials and could shift more barrels into the Midwest in the coming weeks.
Chicago prompt low sulphur diesel late Monday was steady at 1.75/1.50 cents a gallon under NYMEX November heating oil, with high sulphur talked 4.50 cents under the print.

Chicago unleaded gasoline for all October timings was unchanged in late Monday discussion at 0.25 cent under to even with NYMEX November unleaded, with premium talked 3.0 cents higher on the Clark outage.
Group Three prompt low sulphur diesel firmed to 1.0/1.25 cents over the print, with high sulphur unchanged at 2.0 cents under after easing earlier in the day.
Group Three unleaded gasoline for prompt deliveries was talked unchanged at 1.50/1.25 cent under the print, with premium 3.0 cents higher, traders said.
